title: bundle_manifest/v1
description: Identity of one run's evidence bundle, written ONCE at run start and never mutated (immutability beats a mutable status flag; completeness is signaled by chain.json presence + the EpisodeEnd sentinel). Pins the pack (by content hash), the agent (by manifest hash), the engine (exact semver - replay refuses any mismatch, DET-6), and the run configuration (inlined here so the whole replay input is one hashed document). Contains the single permitted wall-clock read (created_at_ms: recorded, never consumed) and the observation time-rebase offset (recorded, never observable by the agent).

schema.description: Schema name and major version of this document.

run_id.description: Harness-generated random run identifier. Identity, not computation: allowed entropy because it never enters the replay function's economics.

episode_id.description: The opaque episode id shown to the agent (observation.episode.episode_id). Recorded here so the bundle discloses the mapping the agent never sees.

created_at_ms.description: Harness wall clock at run start, UTC epoch-ms. THE single permitted wall-clock read in the system: recorded, never consumed (DET-4).

pack.description: Which pack, pinned by content: the auditor's link from evidence to data. Replay refuses a pack whose recomputed content hash differs.

pack_id.description: Pack slug, e.g. 'covid-2020' (operator-side; never in observations).

manifest_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the pack's manifest.json bytes.

agent_manifest_sha256.description: SHA-256 of agent_manifest.json bytes - manifest contents are covered by the chain via this indirection.

engine_version.description: Exact engine/package semver that produced this bundle. tradeevolve replay REQUIRES equality; mismatch is a refusal naming both values, never silent best-effort (DET-6).

spec_versions.description: Map: schema name -> full version used (e.g. {'observation/v1': '1.0.0'}). The compatibility surface replay checks; sourced from spec/schemas/VERSIONS.json at run time.

additionalProperties.description: Full semver of the named schema.

time_rebase_offset_ms.description: Epoch-ms subtracted from real time to produce every observation timestamp: the largest whole multiple of 604800000 (one week) <= pack window start. Preserves time-of-day and weekday, destroys the calendar date (ISO-4). Recorded here for auditors; never observable by the agent (ISO-3).

run_config.description: The run's operator configuration, inlined (rather than a separate file) so the complete replay input is pinned by this one hashed document. The ECONOMIC SEED IS COMPLETE here: starting_nav_micro, the gross leverage cap, the drawdown kill-switch threshold, and the turnover cap are all recorded per run (DET-1/DET-3: replay is a pure function of pack bytes + this object + recorded events; no hidden inputs). Effective-lookback rule: lookback values win over pack defaults when non-null.

starting_nav_micro.description: Starting account capital (NAV at bar 0) in micro-quote units. Part of the frozen replay input: ledger bar-0 NAV and metrics net_return_1e8 are seeded by it, so it MUST be pinned here (DET-1/DET-3). V1 CLI default: 10000000000 (10,000 USDT).

leverage_cap_gross_lev_1e4.description: Account-wide gross leverage cap (sum of |per-market target|) in 1e-4 units, enforced as the lev-gross RiskCheck gate. Protocol default 30000 (3x); recorded per run like turnover_cap_1e8 so every gate limit that appears in observation.risk.constraints exists in this hashed document (SAFE-1).

drawdown_kill_switch_1e8.description: Episode peak-to-trough drawdown threshold in 1e-8 units at which the kill switch flattens all positions (SAFE-3). Protocol default 20000000 (20%); recorded per run so the drawdown-ks constraint limit is pinned in the replay input, matching turnover_cap_1e8's treatment.

lookback_bars.description: Observation trade-bar lookback depth; null = use pack default_lookback.bars. The operator pays the token bill, so the operator's config wins.

funding_prints.description: Observation funding-print lookback; null = use pack default_lookback.funding_prints.

response_deadline_ms.description: Per-attempt agent response budget (IC-6), echoed to the agent in observation.episode.response_deadline_ms. Default 120000. Lives in run config, not the agent manifest: it is an operator budget decision, not an agent attribute.

seed.description: Recorded seed for any permitted randomness (V1 engine uses none; the field exists so any future seeded generator is recorded, DET-4).

items.description: Cost profile name; must exist in the pack's cost_profile_multipliers_1e4.

cost_profiles.description: Cost profiles simulated and stored. V1: ['primary','stress_2x'] - both mandatory so no headline can exist only under the optimistic profile (MATH-5).

turnover_cap_1e8.description: Episode turnover cap (cumulative traded notional / starting NAV, 1e-8 units); null = uncapped (no turnover constraint row appears in observations).

host.description: Informational host provenance; explicitly OUTSIDE the determinism domain - results must not depend on it (DET-3).

ext.description: Sanctioned extension point (see VERSIONING.md). Hashed as-is; values are constrained by schema to JCS-safe types with no fractional numbers ($defs/ext_value).

ext_value.description: JCS-safe extension value (DET-2): null, boolean, string, integer within the I-JSON exact range +/-(2^53-1), or arrays/objects of the same, recursively. A JSON number with a fractional part (e.g. 1.5) is schema-INVALID here - ext contents ride into hashed documents as-is, and no fractional number may enter a hashed document. Boundary note: JSON Schema's 'integer' type admits a mathematically-integral literal such as 1.0; the CI instance scan (float-rejecting JSON parse, see VERSIONING.md) closes that remaining lexical gap.

anyOf.description: JSON string (decimal values ride as strings, e.g. '0.7').
Integer within the I-JSON exact range (JCS round-trips it byte-identically).
Object whose values are all JCS-safe.
